items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿新加坡大奖赛策略失误点评
items.summaryZh: 法拉利承认汉密尔顿因策略失误在新加坡大奖赛中失去领奖台，他最终排名第六。汉密尔顿对自己的策略选择承担全部责任，但法拉利是否应该做更多来挽救他的比赛？
items.originalTitle: Our verdict on Hamilton's Singapore strategy failure
detailZh: 法拉利承认汉密尔顿在新加坡大奖赛中因策略失误失去了领奖台，他最终排名第六。
汉密尔顿对自己的策略选择承担全部责任，但法拉利是否应该做更多来挽救他的比赛，是否能够更好地管理他和队友查尔斯·勒克莱尔？
这里是我们团队的观点...
法拉利（可能）本就注定要输掉这场比赛。
法拉利理所当然地对汉密尔顿的策略成为赛后讨论的焦点感到愤怒，因为内部显然是汉密尔顿的错误，而不是团队的问题。
但这就是当关键信息——即汉密尔顿被告知进站但没有这么做！——因为奇特的法拉利-汉密尔顿无线电死区而没有出现在直播中时会发生的事情。
无论如何，这不是法拉利赢得的比赛，也没有将自己置于最佳获胜位置。我怀疑他们无论如何也没有这样的赛车。
所以，我们真的不应该从相当令人失望的马克斯·维斯塔潘/小红牛的表现中拿走任何东西。汉密尔顿本可以站在杆位。查尔斯·勒克莱尔本可以领先进入第一个弯道。法拉利本可以更好地管理分策略。这些都没有发生！
即使如此，维斯塔潘卓越的轮胎管理——他在第一段练习结束时的速度远远超过任何人在旧轮胎上所能做到的——可能仍然会获胜。
赛道位置是一个需要克服的大障碍，但维斯塔潘和小红牛做到了一切，确保无论其他人是否全力以赴，这都不是问题。
法拉利似乎在任何机会下都能自己给自己添乱。
我实在不明白法拉利在新加坡想要达到什么目标，即使汉密尔顿在推动它。比赛开始时有两种轮胎选择，软胎可以更好地起跑，而中胎可以用于超车，那么为什么当汉密尔顿使用中胎时，他却是最先进维修区的车手？
如果你有两辆赛车，它们的性能水平差不多，而你采取了不同的策略来启动它们，那么车手和车队都需要明白，即使是犹豫一秒钟，也可能迅速让所有的努力付诸东流。
如果一个车手确实比另一个车手快，那么他需要立即做出反应并让对方超越；在队友后面跑超过一圈只会消耗你的轮胎。所以最终，两辆赛车都会受到整体比赛时间的负面影响。
比赛早期，车手和车队需要让不同的策略发挥作用，不要阻碍车手取得尽可能好的成绩，但如果是在接近终点旗的时候，比如说比赛最后10%，那么除了平衡被其他车队车辆追上和超越的风险之外，你应该坚持你的位置。
正如我们在两辆麦凯轮车手之间的冲刺赛中看到的那样，对于车队来说，哪个车手最终排名第四或第五并不重要，但对于其中一位车手来说，贪婪占据了上风。
最后一圈了，奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂基本上被勒克莱尔夹在中间，因为勒克莱尔轮胎出现问题而行驶缓慢，所以兰多·诺里斯也应该考虑到这一点。别提事故了，在车队积分上的损失可能会让迈凯轮损失1000万美元的奖金。
这关乎驾驶员之间的尊重，当你向车队报告你的速度时要有诚实，车队也必须足够大胆，毫不犹豫地做出那些有时困难的决策。
汉密尔顿和法拉利真的步调一致吗？
我对无线电广播的缺失表示同情，这使得事情看起来比实际情况更糟。而且，汉密尔顿在赛后通过车队无线电立即道歉，这很得体。
但这对我在汉密尔顿对法拉利的当前信心上仍留下了一些关键问题。
为什么汉密尔顿在被告知要进站时没有在虚拟安全车下进站？从车内视角来看，他显然没有试图进入维修区——这只能有两个原因。
要么是他简单地忘记了，要么是他否决了法拉利的决定。
如果是后者，这确实引发了关于汉密尔顿是否对法拉利策略师有100%的信任和信心的问题。说实话——谁又能责怪他呢？
我们看到了他的前任，卡洛斯·塞恩斯，在许多场合都做了同样的事情，基本上是从驾驶舱中制定策略。
这可能会造成问题——比如对比赛的完全误判，因为你没有完整的画面——但这是因为被放在错误的位置太多次的后果。
感觉像是从之前的错误中产生的误解可能今天烧毁了法拉利。
detailEn: Ferrari admits Lewis Hamilton lost a podium at Formula 1's Singapore Grand Prix due to a strategy failure which saw him slip back to sixth place.
Hamilton took "full responsibility" for his strategy calls, but should Ferrari have done more to save his race, could it have managed him and team-mate Charles Leclerc better?
Here's what our team thinks...
A race Ferrari (probably) was always going to lose
Ferrari's understandably peeved that Hamilton's strategy became such a big post-race talking point when it seemed internally clear the error was his, not the team's.
But that's what happens when a key bit of information - namely, Hamilton being told to pit but not doing so! - doesn't make it onto the broadcast because of a weird Ferrari-Hamilton radio dead spot.
Regardless, this wasn't a race Ferrari won, or put itself in the best position to win. And I suspect it didn't have the car to anyway.

So really let's not take anything away from a pretty crushing Max Verstappen/Red Bull performance. Hamilton could have been on pole. Charles Leclerc could have led into the first corner. Ferrari could have managed the split-strategy better. None of that happened!
And even if it did, Verstappen's superior tyre management - his pace at the end of the first stint was so far beyond what anyone else could do on old rubber - probably would have won out anyway.

Track position would have been a big hurdle to overcome, but Verstappen and Red Bull did everything right to make sure that was a non-issue regardless of whether others put their best foot forward or not.
Ferrari seems to be able to shoot itself in the foot at any opportunity.

I just don’t understand what Ferrari was trying to achieve in Singapore, even if Hamilton was pushing for it. There was a two-tyre choice to start the race, softs to potentially get off the start line better and mediums to then go long for the overcut, so why, when Hamilton was on mediums, was he the first driver to pit?

If you have two cars and they are more or less at the same performance level and you start them on different strategies, then both the drivers and the team need to understand that indecision, even just for a lap, can put all that effort down the pan very quickly.

If one driver is genuinely faster than the other, then it needs to react and be let past immediately; running behind your team-mate for more than one lap just eats up your tyres. So in the end both cars suffer overall race time.

Early in the race, the drivers and the team need to let the different strategies play out and not stand in the way of a driver getting the best result they can, but if it’s on the run down to the chequered flag, say the last 10% of the race, then other than balancing out the risk of being caught and overtaken by another team's car, you should stick to your positions.
As we saw in the sprint race between the two McLaren drivers, it didn’t really matter to the team which driver was to finish fourth or fifth, but for one of its drivers, greed took over.

It was the last lap, and Oscar Piastri was basically boxed in with Leclerc running slowly with tyre problems, so Lando Norris should have also taken that into account. Never mind the accident, that loss of points in the constructors' could cost McLaren $10million in prize money.
It’s all about respect between drivers, honesty when you're reporting your pace to the team and the team being bold enough to make those sometimes difficult decisions without hesitation.
Are Hamilton and Ferrari really in sync?
I have sympathy for the lack of radio being broadcast, making things look worse than they were. And Hamilton's immediate post-race apology over the team radio was classy.
But it still leaves some key questions for me about Hamilton's current confidence in Ferrari.
Why did Hamilton not pit under the virtual safety car when told to do so? Looking at the onboard, he clearly made no attempt to enter the pits - and that can only be for two reasons.
Either he simply forgot, or he overruled Ferrari.
If it's the latter, that does raise questions about whether Hamilton has 100% faith and trust in Ferrari's strategists. And to be honest - who could blame him?
We saw his predecessor, Carlos Sainz, doing the same on a number of occasions, essentially dictating the strategy from the cockpit.
That will cause problems - like a total misreading of the race because you don't have a full picture - but it's a consequence of being put in the wrong position too many times.
It feels like mistrust from those previous mistakes might have burned Ferrari today.
keyPointsZh: 法拉利可能没有能力赢得比赛。
keyPointsEn: Ferrari may not have had the car to win the race.

items.originalTitle: Winners and losers from F1's Singapore Grand Prix
detailZh: 新加坡大奖赛赢家与输家
Formula 1在新加坡的周末虽然缺乏精彩动作，但仍提供了许多讨论的焦点，从让各自车队失望的车手到一位不断崛起的冠军候选人
查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
残酷的三站赛事最后一站的结果很难预测。随着车手们在赛道上的疲劳累积，常常会有政治阴谋、争吵和人为错误的潜在可能性。
赛道之外，在新加坡周末，事情相对平静，但几位车手可能会希望他们做出了不同的决定。
你可能已经合理地期待本周的头条会是马克斯·维斯塔潘的名字，但在这个可能成为红牛历史上一个重要周末的时候，将鲜花传递给这位荷兰人的信任赛车工程师是公平的。
正如现在众所周知的那样，维斯塔潘将把红牛车队大幅改进的赛车发挥到极致，在车队历史上的噩梦赛道上赢得了一场有控制的胜利，红牛选择让泪流满面的兰比斯站在领奖台上领取车队冠军奖杯，这一举动意义重大，因为这可能是这位英国人在维斯塔潘的赛车工程师生涯中的最后一次胜利。
兰比斯将在最终转会麦克拉伦之前逐渐淡出红牛，汤姆·哈特将成为他的接替者。哈特将在本赛季晚些时候接管麦克风，因此尽管红牛的表现有所回升，但并不能保证强大的维斯塔潘-兰比斯组合会继续增加他们的73场大奖赛胜利数。
如果这是F1历史上最成功的搭档之一结束的方式，那么维斯塔潘和兰比斯以在新加坡大奖赛周末横扫一切的方式谢幕，无线电系统的小故障为这个充满情感的夜晚增添了一丝喜剧色彩。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、兰多·诺里斯、麦克拉伦
坐在法拉利贵宾室的拥挤休息室里，车队老板弗雷德·瓦瑟尔在回答了关于车队新加坡策略的最新一轮问题后显然感到有些尴尬。
似乎没有比法拉利更容易因为其比赛策略而受到指责的团队了，而这种声誉当然部分源于先例。但在社交媒体的喧嚣之外，法拉利在新加坡所尝试的策略中也有一些逻辑。它将软胎起步的查尔斯·勒克莱尔和中等速度的跑者兰多·诺里斯的策略分开，试图对维斯塔潘施加压力，尽管这最终证明是徒劳的，但法拉利仍然处于巩固双料领奖台位置的好位置。
主要问题是新加坡的中胎特别糟糕，这一点通过将两位车手都换上软胎，麦克拉伦已经认识到了，也许法拉利也能消除这一点。但因此让汉密尔顿提前换上磨损的中胎是不可避免的后果。
今天的主要错误是汉密尔顿自己犯的，他在虚拟安全车下被要求进行双停站时拒绝进站。如果他那样做了，车队可能会锁定第二和第三名，而汉密尔顿则承担了在软胎上长时间行驶导致第六名完赛的责任。
‘你昨天问麦克拉伦这么多问题吗？’瓦瑟尔生气了。
兰多·诺里斯，麦克拉伦，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，麦克拉伦
实际上...是的，弗雷德。我们做到了！
这个专栏主要侧重于周日的结果，我们不想给短道赛赋予比其应有的重要性更多的重视。但周六在20圈短道赛最后一圈中，通过兰多·诺里斯对队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里的半心半意的一次冲刺，是令人非常不欢迎的木瓜规则剧情的回归，尤其是在考虑到所涉及的风险如此之小的情况下。
周日，诺里斯似乎表现出更多的悔恨和自我反省，评论他第一次、失败的超越汉密尔顿的尝试，称这是他在周末所犯的几个糟糕决定之一。
车队负责人斯特拉评论说，她在周日看到的诺里斯——主动提出帮助汉密尔顿回到皮亚斯特里身边——与她希望看到的未来形象非常接近。尽管如此，意大利人也确认，在前往美国大奖赛周末之前，还将有更多对话来清除新加坡车队集体系统中的问题。
“我无法尝试我之前做的事情，”诺里斯在比赛后对媒体说，“即使这个动作是可行的，我也从一开始就不应该尝试。我必须更多地考虑我所代表的团队，而不是我自己。这是我的错误，我让团队失望了。”
当被问及他是否对维斯塔潘在积分榜上并没有比他更接近感到高兴时，安东内利回答说：“是的，我知道，那会非常可怕。那会非常、非常可怕。”
即使当他处于赢得锦标赛的边缘时，理论上他可以在奥斯汀的下一场比赛中实现这一点，基米·安东内利也拒绝过度兴奋。
我们在赛季初看到的，是基米·安东内利成长的第一阶段。凭借场上最好的赛车，从发车到终点旗，他展现了纯粹的主导地位。当没有赛车可以击败他时，他被迫进入了一个需要更多成熟度的限制损害的角色，这是第二阶段。”
20岁的年轻人巴库出色的恢复驾驶已经充分说明了他的进步，在马来西亚和新加坡也有同样的表现，即使没有那么耀眼。
这位意大利年轻人令人耳目一新的地方在于，他并没有坚持通常人们在他这个位置上会说的那些虚假的言论。'一场比赛一场比赛来，现在还不考虑冠军，任何事情都可能发生。'
安东内利承认他的首个冠军已经近在咫尺，他利用这一点作为保持敏锐和全速前进的动力，而不是欺骗自己，假装它不存在。'当然，我知道它非常接近，我知道它在那里，'他说。
'但我只是需要确保我继续做到最好。这个周末我并没有特别好的驾驶。我觉得我可以做得更好。但我相信我有时间重新调整。如果我没有做好我的工作，那么结果就不会来。所以为了实现我的目标，我需要表现。就是这样简单。'
我们都知道这里的正确答案是阿斯顿·马丁，而且常读我们文章的读者也知道我们不喜欢在别人处于低谷时还继续打击他们。然而，这条赛道本应该适合AMR26和本田引擎的组合，但当后者不能正常工作时，这也就不算什么了。
整个周末都受到了动力单元相关问题的困扰，这意味着费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔都无法真正竞争，这导致两位车手都从维修区起步，而且无法恢复。
这真的是对马来西亚那更加有希望的周末的一个糟糕的后续，马来西亚的周末为阿隆索和其他车手带来了积分，而其他赛道可能不会提供同样的机会。
detailEn: Winners and losers from F1's Singapore Grand Prix

Formula 1's largely action-starved weekend in Singapore still managed to provide plenty of talking points, from drivers who let their respective teams down to one champion-elect who keeps rising to the occasion
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing
The last leg of a brutal triple-header can really go either way. As fatigue accumulates around the paddock, there is often the potential for political intrigue, bickering and human error.
Off the track, things were relatively well behaved over the Singapore weekend, but a few drivers will be wishing they had made different decisions.

You may have rightly expected the name of Max Verstappen to headline this week's edition, but on what may turn out to be a historic weekend for Red Bull, it's fair to pass the flowers onto the Dutchman's trusted race engineer.

As Verstappen put Red Bull's vastly improved car to good use to snare a controlled victory on the team's historical bogey track, Red Bull's choice to push a tearful Lambiase onto the podium to receive the constructors' trophy is significant because it may well be the Briton's very last win as Verstappen's race engineer.

As is well known by now, Lambiase will be phased out at Red Bull ahead of his eventual McLaren move, with Tom Hart his replacement. Hart will already take over the microphone for a number of races later this season, so despite Red Bull's upturn in form there is no guarantee that the formidable Verstappen-Lambiase combo will add to its tally of 73 grand prix wins.

If this is it for one of the most successful pairings in F1 history, then Verstappen and Lambiase went out in style by sweeping the Singapore sprint weekend, with the radio system hiccup adding a comedic note to an emotional evening.
Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren
Sat in a packed lounge in Ferrari's hospitality, team boss Fred Vasseur clearly felt a bit cornered after the latest barrage of questions on the team's Singapore strategy.

There appears to be no easier team to blame for its race strategy than Ferrari, and some of that reputation is of course steeped in precedent. But far from the madding crowd on social media, there was some logic to what Ferrari was trying to do in Singapore. It split the strategies of soft-starter Charles Leclerc and medium-runner to put some pressure on Verstappen, and when that proved in vain, it was still in a good position to consolidate a double podium.

The main problem was that the medium tyre was particularly rubbish in Singapore, something McLaren recognised by putting both of its drivers on softs, and perhaps something Ferrari could have snuffed out too. But getting Hamilton off the worn medium tyre early was therefore an inevitable consequence.

The main mistake today was made by Hamilton himself, who was called in for a double-stack pitstop under a virtual safety car by refusing to come in. If he had done so, the team would have likely secured second and third, with Hamilton instead taking responsibility for limping home in sixth on an excessively long stint on soft tyres.
"Did you ask this many questions to McLaren, yesterday?" Vasseur bristled.
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren
Actually... yes, Fred. We did!

This column is predominantly weighted towards the result on Sundays, and we don't want to give sprint races any more importance than they really need to get. But Saturday's coming together on the final lap of the 20-lap sprint, through a half-hearted lunge by Lando Norris on team-mate Oscar Piastri, was a very unwelcome return of the papaya rules saga and felt particularly unnecessary given what little was at stake.

On Sunday, Norris appeared to show more contrition and self-reflection, commenting on his first, botched overtake attempt on Hamilton that it was one of several poor decisions he had taken over the weekend.

Team principal Stella commented that the Norris he saw on Sunday - offering his services to help back Hamilton into Piastri - was a hell of a lot closer to the one he wanted to see going forward. Having said that, the Italian also confirmed there will be more conversations heading into the United States Grand Prix weekend to flush Singapore out of the team's collective system.

"I can't attempt what I did," Norris told the press after the race. "I should never have attempted it in the first place, even if the move was on. I've got to think more of the team I represent than myself. It was a mistake on my part, and I let down the team."
Asked if he was happy Verstappen isn't much closer to him in the standings than he is right now, Antonelli replied: "Yeah, I know, because it would be very scary. It would be very, very scary."
Even when he's on the verge of winning the championship, which he could theoretically pull off the next race in Austin, Kimi Antonelli refuses to get overly excited.

What we saw earlier in the season was the first phase of Kimi Antonelli's coming of age. Pure domination from pole to flag with the best car in the field. The next phase arrived when he longer had the car to beat, and was forced into a damage-limiting role which required more maturity.
The 20-year-old's outstanding recovery drive in Baku already spoke volumes about how far he has come, and there was more of the same in Malaysia and Singapore, even if it was less flashy.

What's also refreshing about the Italian youngster is that he's not persisting with the usual bogus lines people tend to trot out in his position. "One race at a time, not thinking about the title yet, anything can happen."

Antonelli acknowledged his maiden title is around the corner now, and uses it as motivation to stay sharp and keep firing on all cylinders rather than fooling himself, pretending it doesn't exist. "For sure. I know it's very close, I know it's there," he said.

"But I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can. This weekend I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job. But I feel confident that I have a week to reset. If I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform. It's as simple as that."

We all know the correct answer here is Aston Martin, and regular readers will also know we don't like to keep kicking the same hard-working people when they're down. However, this is a circuit that should have suited the combination of the AMR26 and the Honda engine, but that doesn't count for much when the latter doesn't work as it should.

The entire weekend was hampered by power unit-related issues which meant neither Fernando Alonso nor Lance Stroll could really compete, triggering pitlane start for both drivers from which there was no recovery.
It really was a poor follow-up to what was a much more promising weekend in Malaysia which yielded points for Alonso, and other circuits may not be offering the same opportunities.

items.originalTitle: Toto Wolff explains the strict transparency keeping Mercedes F1 united
detailZh: Toto Wolff解释了保持梅赛德斯一级方程式车队团结的严格透明度
Toto Wolff拒绝参与维修区政治，坚持乔治·拉塞尔和基米·安东内利之间绝对的透明度
对于梅赛德斯粉丝来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的一级方程式新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析。
随着安德烈亚·基米·安东内利迅速接近2026年世界车手锦标赛，而经验丰富的乔治·拉塞尔在车库里另一边不断面对无情的发车线处罚，梅赛德斯一级方程式车队的内部动态在压力下很容易破裂。然而，车队负责人Toto Wolff积极打造了一个严格建立在平等对待基础上的车库文化，以防止通常摧毁冠军车队的激烈毒性。
沃尔夫那极具透明度的管理风格源于他与四次世界冠军阿兰·普罗斯特的一次关于他在麦克拉伦与艾尔顿·塞纳之间传奇而痛苦的竞争的坦率对话。
在沃尔夫早期作为威廉姆斯的执行官在一级方程式赛道中工作时，他向普罗斯特寻求了解两位天才车手之间关系完全恶化背后的原因。
“在我的F1生涯初期，我在威廉姆斯，”沃尔夫透露。“我对他说，我在电视上看到了整个过程，我以一种近乎天真地问，你们两个是如何几乎在一夜之间升级到这种程度的，因为我并不理解两位车手之间的动态。”
普罗斯特表示，核心问题是维修区在平等地位方面完全缺乏透明度。
“他说问题是你们永远不知道自己是否受到青睐，”沃尔夫回忆道。‘他说有时候我觉得，你知道，是我……然后在不同年份的不同阶段，是塞纳受到青睐。他还说这造成了团队中的不信任氛围，你感觉你的直接对手可能被给予了优势。’
“因为现代赛车手在他们的成长年份完全依靠个人的生存本能参加高度紧张的青训车队，沃尔夫认为车队经理必须积极提供一个安全、平衡的心理环境，其中不存在偏袒。”
“最后，这些车手就像被放在卡丁车上的八岁小孩一样有些受惊。他们感到害怕；这是父母们追逐的梦想。天气潮湿，你需要比赛，然后最终你进入了一级方程式，他们告诉你，你知道，现在你必须玩团队游戏。”"
“为了防止破坏普罗斯-塞纳动态的不信任，沃尔夫在梅赛德斯维修区建立了一套严格的绝对诚实和平等规则。”"
“你需要感受到车队在情感上的保护，”沃尔夫表示，“如果你做不到这一点，并且保持透明和平衡，这可能会创造一些车手失去信心的时刻。”
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯，乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯，托托·沃尔夫，梅赛德斯
如果车队需要正式调整其策略，并明确偏向安东内利而非拉塞尔以确保2026年车手锦标赛的胜利，沃尔夫保证他不会在幕后或通过含糊不清的无线电信息隐藏这一策略。车队的两边都将被公开且平等地告知。
“对我来说，从那次学习来看，是可以的；我永远不能那样做。我需要保持透明，”沃尔夫声明，“如果有一天我们决定以任何形式玩团队游戏，我会说的。我会说，现在这些是规则，我们将非常开放和透明。如果我们因为车手不同意而进行讨论……那么好吧，我们就进行讨论。”
通过确保两位车手都不会猜测他们在内部等级制度中的位置，沃尔夫意图在赛季最后几轮比赛中保持梅赛德斯车队的完全统一。
detailEn: Toto Wolff explains the strict transparency keeping Mercedes F1 united
Toto Wolff refuses to play paddock politics, insisting on absolute transparency between George Russell and Kimi Antonelli
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

With Andrea Kimi Antonelli rapidly closing in on the 2026 world drivers' championship and veteran George Russell battling through relentless grid penalties on the opposite side of the garage, the internal dynamics at the Mercedes F1 Team could easily fracture under the pressure. However, team principal Toto Wolff has actively engineered a garage culture strictly built on equal treatment to prevent the intense toxicity that often destroys championship-winning squads.

The foundation for Wolff's fiercely transparent management style stems directly from a revealing grid conversation he had with four-time world champion Alain Prost regarding his legendary, bitter rivalry with Ayrton Senna at McLaren.

During Wolff's early years in the Formula 1 paddock as an executive at Williams, he approached Prost to understand exactly how the relationship between two generational talents completely deteriorated.

"It was very early in my Formula 1 life; I was at Williams," Wolff revealed. "I said to him, I saw it on TV the whole thing, and I said how did that escalate between the two of you almost in a naive way, because I didn't understand the dynamics between the two drivers."
According to Prost, the core issue was a complete lack of transparency from the pitwall regarding equal status.

"He said the problem was that you never knew whether you were favoured," Wolff recounted. "He said at times I felt that, you know, it was me... and then at different stages of the years it was Senna who was favoured. And he said that created a dynamic of mistrust in the team, and you felt that your direct opponent may be given advantages."

Because modern racing drivers spend their formative years relying entirely on individual survival instincts in highly pressurised junior series, Wolff believes a team principal must actively provide a secure, balanced psychological environment where favouritism doesn't exist.

"At the end, the drivers are little traumatised eight-year-olds that were put in a go-kart," Wolff explained. "They were scared; it was a parent's dream that they were chasing. It's wet, and you need to race, and then eventually you end up in Formula 1, and they tell you, you know, now you have to play the team game."
To prevent the mistrust that destroyed the Prost-Senna dynamic, Wolff established a strict rule of absolute honesty and equality inside the Mercedes garage.
"You need to feel emotionally protected by the team," Wolff stated. "If you don't do that and you keep it transparent and balanced, that can create moments where the driver just loses confidence."
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes

If the team ever needs to officially pivot its strategy and explicitly favour Antonelli over Russell to secure the 2026 Drivers' Championship, Wolff guarantees he will not hide the strategy behind closed doors or vague radio messages. Both sides of the garage will be informed openly and equally.

"From that learning for me, it was OK; I can never do that. I need to be transparent," Wolff declared. "And if one day we decide to play the team game in whatever form, I will say so. I will say, these are the rules now, and we'll be very open and transparent. And if we have a discussion because the driver disagrees... then fine, let's have the discussion."
By ensuring neither driver ever has to guess where they stand in the internal hierarchy, Wolff intends to keep the Mercedes garage completely unified as they head into the final rounds of the season.

items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿新加坡大奖赛意外崩溃原因
items.summaryZh: 汉密尔顿在新加坡大奖赛中因未在虚拟安全车阶段进站而失误，导致赛车崩溃。他在比赛中从第三位跌至第六位，而队友勒克莱尔和安东内利则趁机在短暂的安全车阶段进站。
items.originalTitle: Why Hamilton's Singapore GP really imploded
detailZh: 汉密尔顿在新加坡大奖赛中因未在虚拟安全车阶段进站而失误，导致赛车崩溃。
汉密尔顿在新加坡大奖赛的前半段跑在队友查尔斯·勒克莱尔之后，位列第三，但他的赌注——坚持使用旧款软胎跑完全程——最终失败了。
勒克莱尔和基米·安东内利利用兰斯·斯特罗尔的阿斯顿·马丁赛车故障引发的短暂安全车阶段的机会进行了便宜的进站。
如果汉密尔顿也这样做，他可能会在几圈前进站并利用提前进站策略超越兰多·诺里斯。
由于他没有这样做，车队无线电中只有勒克莱尔被指示进站的指令，这似乎表明法拉利在VSC期间不可思议地将汉密尔顿排除在外。
鉴于汉密尔顿在第一段比赛中使用了更硬的轮胎组合，而在其他两位车手进站更换中胎后，他仍然使用软胎，这似乎尤为奇怪。
这意味着他只能进行一次进站，这将导致第二段比赛时间过长，这是不切实际的。
但这却是由于一个不寻常的故障导致的误导性后果，该故障阻止了法拉利在VSC期间以及之后与汉密尔顿的无线电通讯被听到。
他的车载摄像头和音频在VSC开始后不久就出现了明显的扭曲。法拉利坚称，汉密尔顿在16号弯时被指示——与勒克莱尔同时——但他没有这么做。
在VSC期间结束后的一段时间内，没有收到来自或发给汉密尔顿的无线电信息。这通常伴随着一条消息，告知VSC即将结束，以确保车手准备好重新开始比赛——因此，这与某种奇怪的事情发生，阻止了汉密尔顿的无线电信号被捕捉（这有时会发生）的观点是一致的。
无论是什么问题，几分钟后就自行解决了。汉密尔顿在比赛结束时通过无线电向法拉利道歉，因为他关于策略的判断是错误的。
汉密尔顿无法在赛后澄清情况，因为他没有进行电视或书面媒体任务。法拉利表示他感到不适，在接受了FIA医疗团队的检查后，被允许不参加赛后媒体区。
但是瓦瑟尔——他对在常规媒体简报中被频繁询问这个话题感到沮丧——说：“我们叫了两辆车。‘伙计们，你们在VSC后面进维修区。’我的一个家伙说，‘不，我更喜欢留在赛道上。’
他说，‘我错过了进维修区的入口。’不要责怪车队。
法拉利后来发布的一段汉密尔顿的话中，他只说‘车队叫我进维修区，但我错过了入口’，并且他在车队无线电中也传达了类似的信息——如果字面意思是‘错过’，那么如果他事先得到了很多警告，却在最后一刻没有明显尝试进入维修区，这似乎会很奇怪。
可能汉密尔顿实际上只是选择留在赛道上，但结果是一样的。
这使得汉密尔顿处于明显的劣势，他通过争论试图让一次进站策略得以实施，但这反而巩固了糟糕的结果，因为他在比赛中使用了比其他任何领跑者都要长的10圈软胎。
几圈之后，法拉利试图让汉密尔顿在正常赛车条件下进站，并改为两次进站策略。这将使他失去赛道位置，但至少汉密尔顿在比赛末段会有更新的轮胎，并且有多圈的时间差来尝试追上安东内利和两辆迈凯轮。
法拉利表示，他距离实现一次进站策略还有6圈，但汉密尔顿认为，如果他进站就会失去两个位置，那么坚持等待并看看是否会有黄旗出现可能是有价值的。
他被允许尝试，但失败了。尽管他的软胎在一开始表现良好，但它们逐渐减弱，然后在最后10圈急剧下降。
在这个阶段，汉密尔顿的每圈时间都在1分38.6秒或更慢。他所竞争的赛车在这个阶段每圈快了1到2秒，速度损失如此严重，以至于甚至需要因慢漏气而进行计划外第二次停车的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，也能在最后追上并超过汉密尔顿。
汉密尔顿将其描述为“痛苦的一课，但我对所做的决定承担全部责任。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton’s Singapore Grand Prix imploded after his error in failing to pit during the mid-race virtual safety car period as Ferrari instructed him to.
Hamilton ran third behind team-mate Charles Leclerc in the first half of the Singapore race but slumped to sixth as his gamble on staying on old soft tyres to the end of the race backfired.
Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli took the opportunity to make a cheap pitstop during the brief VSC period sparked by Lance Stroll’s stricken Aston Martin.
Had Hamilton done the same, he would likely have emerged just ahead of Lando Norris, who had pitted a few laps before the VSC and gained ground with the undercut.
As he did not, and team radio only existed of Leclerc being instructed to pit, it seemed as though Ferrari had inexplicably left Hamilton out during the VSC.
This appeared doubly odd given Hamilton was on softs - with the other two pitting to switch from mediums - after running the harder compound in the opening stint.
So running a one-stop to the end would mean an unrealistically long second stint.
But that was the misleading consequence of an unusual fault that prevented Ferrari’s radio communications with Hamilton through and shortly after the VSC period from being heard.
His onboard camera and audio suffered a clear distortion shortly after the VSC began. Ferrari is adamant that Hamilton was instructed - at the same time as Leclerc - around Turn 16, but he did not.

There were no radio messages to or from Hamilton for a short while, even when the VSC period ended. This is always met with a message that the VSC is ending to make sure the driver is ready to resume racing - so it is consistent with the notion that something odd happened to prevent Hamilton’s radio from being captured, not just muted (which sometimes happens).
Whatever issue there was resolved itself after a few minutes. Hamilton apologised to Ferrari on the radio at the end of the race for his call on the strategy being wrong.

Hamilton was not able to clarify the situation post-race as he did not conduct television or written media duties. Ferrari said he felt unwell and, after being seen by the FIA medical team, was given permission not to attend the post-race media pen.

But Vasseur - who grew frustrated about being asked so many questions about the topic in his regular media debrief - said: “We called two cars. ‘Guys, you pit behind the VSC.’ One of my guys said, ‘no, I prefer to stay on track’.
“He said, ‘I missed the pit entry’. Don't blame the team.”

In a quote from Hamilton later issued by Ferrari, he only said “the team called me in but I missed the entry”, and he did relay a similar message over the team radio - if meant literally 'missed', it would seem odd if he was told with plenty of warning and made no obvious attempt to get into the pitlane at the last moment.
It may be that Hamilton actually just chose to stay out, but the outcome was the same.

It put Hamilton at a clear disadvantage and he doubled down by arguing to try to make the one-stop work from there only solidified a poor result as he ran the softs 10 laps longer than any of the other frontrunners did during the race.

A few laps later, Ferrari tried to get Hamilton to pit in normal racing conditions and switch to a two-stop. This would have cost him track position, but at least Hamilton would have had fresher tyres for the end of the race plus a multi-lap offset to try to come back at the likes of Antonelli and the two McLarens.

Ferrari said he was six laps short of making a one-stop viable, but Hamilton argued if he was already going to lose two positions with a pitstop it could be worth trying to hold on and see if another caution period occurred.
He was told he could try, but it failed. Though his softs held on well for a while, they steadily faded and then fell away sharply in the final 10 laps.

In this period, every lap of Hamilton’s was 1m38.6s or slower. The cars he was racing were between 1-2s faster per lap in this period, and the loss of pace was so severe that even Oscar Piastri, who required an unplanned second stop for a slow puncture, was able to catch and pass Hamilton late on.
Hamilton described it as a “painful lesson, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made”.

items.originalTitle: Why Ferrari caved in to Lewis Hamilton’s failed Singapore F1 gamble
detailZh: 法拉利车队主管弗雷德·瓦瑟尔在新加坡大奖赛赛后面对媒体，热门话题是刘易斯·汉密尔顿。
大部分问题围绕着他因选择错误策略，从第三位跌至第六位，在滨海湾赛道上坚持使用软胎完成44圈长距离赛段。
作为法拉利车队主管，弗雷德·瓦瑟尔在新加坡大奖赛赛后面对媒体，讨论的焦点是刘易斯·汉密尔顿。
大多数问题都集中在汉密尔顿因选择错误策略，从第三位跌至第六位，他在滨海湾赛道上坚持使用软胎完成了44圈的长距离赛段。
在过去的22场比赛中，经过中和后，汉密尔顿相对于法拉利车队队友查尔斯·勒克莱尔，平均每圈损失了2.5秒。这就是他最终排在基米·安东内利和迈凯轮车队之后的第六位。
由于生病的英国人免除了赛后媒体承诺前往医疗中心，瓦瑟尔面临记者的审查，他们渴望了解这一决定是如何做出的，细节到了最高水平。而且法国人并不享受这种前景；他甚至打断第一个问题，暗示这并不一定是“周末的大事件”。
无论如何，汉密尔顿赛后的无线电道歉清楚地表明，他在VSC期间做出了留在赛道上的决定——那么这场讨论究竟是如何进行的呢？
“[它]非常清楚，”瓦瑟尔坚持说。“我们在赛道上是第二到第三位。我们叫了两辆车，‘伙计们，你们在VSC后面进站’。我的一个家伙说，‘不，我更喜欢留在赛道上’。或者说他没有说——他说，‘我错过了进站入口’。
“不要责怪车队。”
瓦瑟尔，他还没有和他的车手交谈，表示汉密尔顿的决定是“显然是一个错误”，强化了他之前对广播员的说法。
但是，如果车手没有像工程师那样拥有详尽的数据和全局视角，他是否可以推翻车队的策略？
“当你看到结果时，这显然不是一个好的决定，”瓦瑟尔承认。“但另一方面，你也很经常告诉我们，我们必须听从车手，因为他们坐在车里，他们对轮胎有感觉等等。”
“但是我认为在这件事上对我来说很清楚。但我也要尊重他们在车内时的感受。”
法拉利随后发布了一份汉密尔顿的声明——弥补了他在赛后媒体区的缺席——在这份声明中，这位七届世界冠军将这次挫折描述为“痛苦的教训”。
“今天的结果并不是我们想要的，这责任在我，”汉密尔顿被引用说。“在一个难以超车的赛道上，你需要尝试不同的方法，我选择使用新的中等硬度轮胎，尝试长距离行驶并尝试一次停站策略。不幸的是，中等硬度轮胎的表现并没有像软胎那样好。
“我在第二段比赛中表现不错，速度也回来了，但我没有取得我需要的进步。在虚拟安全车期间，车队叫我进站，但我错过了入口。之后，我决定留在赛道上，试图保持到最后，但在最后几圈，我因为轮胎磨损严重而挣扎，失去了三个位置，最终排名第6，这并不反映我们今天在车上的速度。”
“今天是一个痛苦的教训，但我对所做的决定承担全部责任。并不是每个决定都会成功，我可以接受犯错，但我为今天失去的积分向车队道歉。他们每个周末都投入了这么多，我想为他们做得更多。”
“我将继续努力，并在下一场比赛中战斗回来。”
detailEn: Why Ferrari caved in to Lewis Hamilton’s failed Singapore F1 gamble
Lewis Hamilton lost three places to a poor strategy he picked himself at Marina Bay; Fred Vasseur explains how it happened
As Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur faced the media following Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, the hot topic was Lewis Hamilton.

Most of the questions revolved around the unsuccessful strategy that saw Hamilton collapse from third to sixth in the Marina Bay race, as he stayed out under the VSC to complete a mammoth 44-lap stint on soft tyres.

Across the last 22 of those, following the neutralisation, Hamilton haemorrhaged 2.5s a lap on average relative to Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc. That is how he ended up sixth behind Kimi Antonelli and the McLarens.

With the unwell Briton exempted from his post-race media commitments to visit the medical centre instead, Vasseur faced scrutiny from journalists keen to establish how that decision was made to the highest level of detail. And the Frenchman wasn’t enjoying that prospect; he even interrupted the first question, suggesting it wasn’t necessarily “the big event of the weekend”.
Regardless, Hamilton’s post-race radio apology made it clear that he had made the call to stay out during the VSC – so how exactly did that discussion pan out?

“[It] was very clear,” Vasseur insisted. “We were P2-P3 on the track. We called two cars, ‘Guys, you pit behind the VSC’. One of my guys said, ‘No, I prefer to stay on track’. Or he didn’t say – he said, ‘I missed the pit entry’.
“Don't blame the team.”
Vasseur, who was yet to speak to his driver, said Hamilton’s decision was “clearly a mistake”, doubling down on what he previously told broadcasters.
But is it OK for a driver to override the team’s strategy, given he does not have the same exhaustive data and global view as engineers do?

“When you see the outcome, it was not a good call,” Vasseur admitted. “But on the other hand, quite often you are also telling us that we have to listen to the drivers, because they are into the car, they have the feeling with their tyres and so on.
“But I think on this one it was clear for me. But I have also to respect their feeling when they are into the car.”
Ferrari subsequently provided a statement from Hamilton – making up for his absence in the post-race media pen – in which the seven-time world champion described the setback as a “painful lesson”.

“Today wasn’t the result we were looking for and it was on me,” Hamilton was quoted as saying. “At a track that’s difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work. Unfortunately, the medium didn’t perform as well as the soft.

“I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn’t make the progress I needed. Under the VSC, the team called me in but I missed the entry. After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but, in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car today.

“A painful lesson today, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I’m sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them.
“I’ll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race.”

keyPointsEn: Fred Vasseur explained how the situation occurred

items.originalTitle: How Kimi Antonelli will cope with pressure of clinching F1 title at US GP
detailZh: 如何应对在美国大奖赛上赢得F1冠军的压力
梅赛德斯车手科米·安东内利可能将在奥斯汀赢得他个人的F1世界冠军
F1冠军领跑者科米·安东内利誓言在即将到来的美国大奖赛中保持同样的心态，在那里他可能赢得他个人的世界冠军
梅赛德斯车手科米·安东内利是2026年的统治性表现者，他领先队友乔治·拉塞尔102分，这得益于14个领奖台，包括8个胜利。
安东内利最近一次的成绩是在周日的新加坡站获得第三名，这意味着他现在有机会在下一站的美国赛车场赢得冠军。
为了实现这一目标，他必须获胜并希望拉塞尔排名第九或更低，其他情况最有可能将比赛推迟到十月底的墨西哥，因此在奥斯汀发生的可能性很小。
当在滨海湾被问及他是否会在奥斯汀考虑冠军时，这位20岁的年轻人回答道：“当然。但与此同时，我知道这非常接近，我知道它就在那里，但我只是需要确保我继续做到最好。
“我的心态始终如一，那就是出去赢得比赛并以我能做到的最佳方式表现。我认为这个周末我并没有特别驾驶得很好。我觉得我可以做得更好。
“但我感觉很有信心，你知道的，一周的休息时间，我非常期待回到奥斯汀。”
“最终，如果我没有做好我的工作，那么结果就不会来。所以为了实现我想要的目标，我需要像那样简单地表现。”
他的冠军争夺战的基础在赛季早期就奠定了，因为梅赛德斯在规则变更的开关中取得了主导地位，通过从杆位赢得前六轮比赛，安东内利赢得了五场胜利。”
随后法拉利和迈凯轮安装了各种升级来缩小差距，这意味着安东内利在接下来的九轮比赛中只赢得了三场，直到九月的巴库更新后，红牛车队才加入竞争。”
马克斯·维斯塔潘因此从杆位赢得了最后两场比赛，以及新加坡短道赛，而梅赛德斯仍在试图弄清楚上周日在吉隆坡带来的更新。
安东内利可以感谢红牛今年开局缓慢，前五轮只有一次领奖台，否则四次世界冠军维斯塔潘的威胁会更高。
“那会非常可怕，”他告诉天空体育，当被问及维斯塔潘在这个阶段落后119分以下的可能性时。
“那会非常、非常可怕。但总的来说，我觉得我们在做得很棒。最后，你看整个赛季，我们一直都在那里。
“显然，我们一直有一辆出色的赛车，现在我们正在尝试理解这个新套件，但我非常为这个周末的团队感到骄傲，因为我们克服了困难，并开始看到隧道尽头的曙光。”
“这只是时间问题。现在我们再次回到奥斯汀。一个正常的周末，标准的周末，我们希望进行很多改变，并更好地理解这个套件。”
detailEn: How Kimi Antonelli will cope with pressure of clinching F1 title at US GP
The Mercedes driver could clinch his maiden F1 world title at Austin next time out
Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli has vowed to keep the same mindset for the United States Grand Prix, where he could clinch his maiden world title.
The Mercedes driver has been the dominant performer of 2026 as he holds a 102-point gap over team-mate George Russell in second, thanks to 14 podiums including eight wins.
Antonelli’s most recent result was third at Singapore on Sunday and it means he now has his first opportunity of clinching the title at Circuit of the Americas next time out.
To do so he must win and hope Russell finishes ninth or lower with anything else most likely taking the fight to Mexico at the end of October, so the chances of it happening in Austin are slim.

When asked at Marina Bay if he will be thinking of the title at Austin, the 20-year-old replied: “For sure. But at the same time, I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can.
“The mindset is always the same to go out there and win and perform the best way I can. I think this weekend I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job.
“But I feel confident that, you know, a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to be back in Austin.
“At the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform as simple as that.”
The foundations of his title charge came early in the season as Mercedes made a dominant start to the regulation switch by winning the opening six rounds from pole, Antonelli taking five victories.
Ferrari and McLaren subsequently fitted various upgrades to close the gap, meaning Antonelli won only three of the next nine rounds before a Baku update in September saw Red Bull enter the fray.
Max Verstappen has therefore won the last two races from pole, as well as the Singapore sprint, while Mercedes is still trying to figure out the update it brought to Sepang last weekend.

So Antonelli can be thankful that Red Bull made a slow start to the year, with just one podium in the opening five rounds, otherwise the threat from four-time world champion Verstappen would be higher.
“It would be very scary,” he told Sky Sports, when asked about the possibility of Verstappen being less than 119 points behind at this stage.
“It would be very, very scary. But all in all I feel like we're doing a great job. At the end, you look at the season and we've always been there.

“So obviously we've had a great car and now we're trying to understand this new package but I'm very proud of the team this weekend because we pushed through the difficulties and we started to see the light at the end of the tunnel.
“So it's just a matter of time. Now we go back to Austin again. A normal weekend, standard weekend, where we can hopefully do a lot of changes and understand more of this package.”
keyPointsZh: 他可能在美国大奖赛中夺得首个世界冠军
keyPointsEn: He could win his first world championship at the United States Grand Prix
